Rests on a premise about ci/delta.is_engine not verifiable from the bundle; placing the module outside l7r/ to honor 'as tooling' literally is a design choice, not a fidelity finding.

decisions.summary: Exits: 'FR-008 green: landed with its fresh rate. Red: the failing seeds recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be placed correctly ruled through make arbiter-ask (D11, D35).'
decisions.why: Template text from another feature: FR-008 is 'the engine stays in Python', not a landing condition; D11 and D35 exist nowhere in this plan or spec-cited.md; 'placed correctly' and 'fresh rate' are placement/seed-pass language for a tool that changes no stage. As written, the red exit sets T01 down on 'failing seeds'. T01 cannot make a seed regress (FR-007), so the only failing seeds at its landing are ones already failing on HEAD, and request.md 4 ('should not require all seeds to pass if seeds were previously failing') and 5 ('not have a requirement to have all of our seeds pass') exclude exactly that as a reason. It abandons the requested survey on a condition the GM ruled out: not physically necessary, not implied by the GM's words (they say the opposite), not serving the purpose. Fix: green = tests red without D1 and make perf-fanout on the current engine compared with research/fanout-2026-10-26.txt (FR-001, SC-001); red = only a seed passing on HEAD that fails after (FR-007); strike FR-008, D11, D35, 'placed correctly', 'fresh rate'.

decisions.why: Restates the approach the GM approved in request.md 5, in its order.

decisions.summary: D1 prints the multiplier chains only for each stage of 300,000 calls or more at the larger size
decisions.why: SC-001 (cited in full) requires the output to list EVERY chain of 50k+ calls with its anchor, and the plan's own Performance Goals restates that, but D1's stage gate cannot reach a function called 50,000-299,999 times in a stage whose total is under 300,000: such a chain is never printed. The GM named this range himself (request.md 2: 'hundreds of thousands or millions of times'), and FR-002 scopes every engine task against this output, so a skipped chain is a hotspot no task is ever scoped against - the gate defeats the survey's purpose. Walking every stage is not impossible, the GM's words do not imply the gate, and 'kept as written there' in the design note does not override SC-001. Fix: the stage gate becomes HOT (any stage holding a non-builtin function called HOT or more times at the larger size gets its chains), or there is no stage gate; the walk itself stays as written. If the author holds that the 300,000 gate is right, that is a spec amendment of SC-001 for the GM's review, not a plan decision.

decisions.summary: JOBS defaults to 3 rather than the design note's 5, citing the shared memory cap
decisions.why: An overridable concurrency default; it changes nothing the tool reports. Its memory figures carry date and method (the memory watch, 2026-10-26).

The GM's request names no landing route, make land is the stricter route, and the design note's own file location under l7r/ is what closes the tooling route. Nothing the GM gets is narrowed.

decisions.summary: make perf adds a separate counting pass after the timed rolls: same seeds (and sizes under SCALING=1), sys.monitoring PY_START counter on tool id 3, per-stage per-seed calls and the snapshot's versions recorded
decisions.why: Request 4: 'record call counts alongside the timings'; a separate pass keeps the timings the GM said to keep recording undistorted. FR-006 adopts call-count-flag.md; tool id is mechanism.

decisions.summary: Counts are of Python functions only; shapely/numpy C work is not counted
decisions.why: The GM adopted the session's measure ('do as you say and record call counts'); FR-006 defers to call-count-flag.md, and D1's survey counts the same Python-level calls. A definition of the metric, not a carve-out from it.

decisions.summary: Counting pass overhead measured on the reference seeds and recorded beside the code; a test rolls one stage twice and asserts equal counts
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested gate: the GM chose counts 'because ... that is consistent'; the test only fails if they are not.

decisions.summary: perf_review.check, run by the push, compares the newest -start/-end pair's counts seed by seed and stage by stage
decisions.why: Request 4: 'that flag would replace the timing band' - the count check stands where the band check stood. The bundle does not let me confirm the band's own reach, so this is classed on the request's framing of replacement in place.

decisions.summary: A -start/-end pair on different versions (interpreter, numpy, shapely) is 'not compared', never flagged, and the push proceeds
decisions.why: Request 4: 'the call counts themselves are the thing that we are gating on', and an increase 'would need to be accepted by the arbiter'. Applying the gate to a cross-version pair is neither impossible nor purpose-defeating: it costs one arbiter call, and the arbiter can see the versions differ ('the kind of thing that I would expect the arbiter to be able to handle without me'). The carve-out resolves 'the delta cannot be attributed' by not watching at all, so any engine increase lands unwatched whenever a dependency bump sits between -start and -end. Should say: a pair on different versions is not compared AND the push refuses until a comparable pair exists (the -start re-rolled on the current versions) or the arbiter rules on it under the same <NNN>-calls subject - never a silent pass.

decisions.summary: The line: over 5% in any stage on any seed (CALLS_STAGE_LINE) or 2% in the total (CALLS_TOTAL_LINE), GUESS knobs with the reason beside them
decisions.why: The GM: the count flag 'would replace the timing band' and arbiter attention 'if it is increasing by too much'; FR-006 and SC-005 say 'over the line'. Values are labeled knobs, not measured claims.

decisions.summary: Over-the-line increase with no arbiter accept refuses the push and names make arbiter-ask SUBJECT=<NNN>-calls with stages, seeds, counts; an accept in arbiter.jsonl clears it; a decrease is printed and needs nothing
decisions.why: Request 4 ('would need to be accepted by the arbiter'); FR-006; SC-005 (refuses and names the arbiter command; accepted lands with the ruling recorded).

decisions.summary: Timings printed for information only; no rule acts on them; the band FLAG retired, perf_bands keeps only what printing needs
decisions.why: Request 4: 'keep recording the timings, but completely stop using timings as a gate on anything'; SC-005.

decisions.summary: pass overhead measured and recorded; a test asserts equal counts on two rolls of one stage

decisions.summary: perf_review.check compares the newest -start/-end pair's counts seed by seed and stage by stage
decisions.why: FR-006 / SC-005: call counts are what is watched.

decisions.summary: CHANGED: a pair on different interpreter/library versions is not compared and REFUSES the push until a comparable pair (the -start re-taken) exists or the round arbiter rules on the <NNN>-calls subject; it never passes silently
decisions.why: The earlier text let a version-mismatched pair pass unflagged, a hole through which an increase could land without the arbiter (FR-006: an increase over the line 'owes the round arbiter's acceptance before it lands'). The new text closes it: nothing passes unexamined, and the way out is the arbiter or a comparable measurement, as the GM wanted (request 4: 'accepted by the arbiter ... the kind of thing that I would expect the arbiter to be able to handle without me'). It is enforcement of the requested watch, not a narrowing and not new behavior beyond it.
